label: Early copy-phase steps (outputs 1-3) of long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or the <DEL> step. Concentrated on the first few copy steps (recall_idx 1-3, i.e. input = original token 0-2 fed back), with recall_idx 2 strongest (46% of mass, the step whose two-back input is <DEL>). Rate rises steeply with sequence length: L=9 holds 63% of mass, L<=5 is essentially silent, so it effectively tracks many outputs still to go (to_go 4-7). Magnitude is also modulated by which token is fed back: b, j, z, n, 0, i, f, 1 give much higher rates (b 3.7x lift; top examples are mostly b at the second copy step), vowels like a/e/o and k/m/p/r/w are weak. A small secondary bump appears at the last copy steps of L=9 sequences (t=16-17). Predicate captures ~81% of mass but precision is under 0.5 because many early-copy steps with non-preferred tokens stay inactive; token-set restrictions trade recall for precision without raising F1.
